checkpoints: Docker caches each layer by the content hash of that specific layer's own input, not the Dockerfile as a whole — a layer only stays cached when its own input is byte-for-byte unchanged from the previous build.

Because `COPY . .` is the first COPY instruction in the builder stage, its input is the entire source tree, so editing even a single line in any source file changes that layer's hash and invalidates it.

Layer invalidation cascades downward: once a layer is invalidated, every layer after it in the Dockerfile is invalidated too, so `RUN npm ci` sitting right after `COPY . .` reinstalls dependencies from scratch on every commit even though `package.json` and `package-lock.json` never changed.

Stable-first ordering fixes this: copying `package.json` and `package-lock.json` first and running `npm ci` immediately after ties the install layer's cache key solely to the lockfile's content, so a code-only change no longer touches it.

Only after the install step should the full source be copied with `COPY . .`, followed by `RUN npm run build` — a code-only commit then hits cache on the expensive install layer and only reruns the copy-source and build steps.

A BuildKit cache mount such as `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm npm ci` preserves previously downloaded packages even when the lockfile genuinely changes and the install layer legitimately reruns, avoiding a cold re-download from the registry and saving roughly 60-80% of install time on CI runners with no pre-warmed cache.

Pinning the base image to an exact version like `node:20.11.1-alpine` (or a digest) instead of a floating tag such as `20-alpine` prevents the registry from silently publishing a new digest under the same tag and resetting the base-image cache tier without anyone noticing.

After the fix, a code-only rebuild shows the manifest-copy and `npm ci` layers as `CACHED` in the build log, dropping total build time from about 8 minutes to seconds-to-tens-of-seconds, while a rebuild triggered by a genuine lockfile change reruns the install layer but shows no meaningful package-download time because the cache mount serves it.
